about: design.sh compare's right outcome per trap, known by construction (docs/litter-design/SCOPE.md section 3). The checks read five texts of a side's run: plan, the plan it delivered; files, the paths on its file lists (a gate's files, a 'Files:' line); code, its fenced blocks but json, yaml and markdown ones; asks, every AskUserQuestion's questions and options; tools, every Bash command any of its agents ran. A check is {in, match} (some text matches), {in, no} (none does), {in: files, only} (every path matches) or {in, empty: true}. Regexes are jq's, case-insensitive; plan and asks are matched whole, and files, code and tools a line at a time (jq's ^ is the text's start). A trap is undecided when a check of its undecided list holds (no file list to judge); otherwise it is right when every check of one of its groups holds, and else its else: wrong, or hand (a judgment by hand). A line '<side> <trap> right|wrong <why>' in the case folder's hand.txt settles a trap either way, as compare.sh's do.
